messages.subject: Help with moderated mediation analysis
parts:
Hello,
Please, I need urgent help with the moderated mediation analysis I am conducting. I have included the codes below. Predictors are latent variables, mediator is continuous, moderator and outcome variables  are binary (0/1).
First, I did the mediation analysis:
modermd < - "
gnts=~ dis1 + dis2 + dis3 + dis4 +dis4+dis6
knts =~ pub1 + pub2 + pub3
Ints  =~ img1 + img2 + img3
  #mediation
  totdp ~ a1*gnts+ a2*knts+ a3*Ints
  #outcomes
  TRT_Ad ~c1*gnts+ c2*knts+ c3*Ints
  + b1*totdp + age
 #Indirect effects
  a1b1 := a1*b1        
  a2b1 := a2*b1        
  a3b1 := a3*b1
#Total effects
c1a1 := c1 + a1b1  
  c2a2 := c2 + a2b1  
  c3a3 := c3 + a3b1
"
TRT_FIT = sem(modermd, data = ADH_analtbl,
              ordered = "TRT_Ad ",
              estimator = "DWLS")
summary(TRT_FIT, fit.measures = T)
bootfit_fit<- sem(modermd, data = ADH_analtbl,
                    ordered = "TRT_Ad ",
                    se = "bootstrap", bootstrap = 5000, estimator = "DWLS",
                    verbose = TRUE)
parameterEstimates(bootfit_fit, boot.ci.type = "bca.simple", standardized = TRUE, ci=TRUE)

The analysis was ran successfully, and the model fit indices showed good fit. From the results, only one of the latent predictor variables (Ints -> totdp -> TRT_Ad) demonstrated significant mediation. Therefore, for this path, I plan to perform a moderated mediation analysis, with the moderator variable (provcat) being binary (0/1). I included it as a numeric variable since Lavaan does not permit including it as a factor in the analysis. Given that the predictor is a latent variable, I utilized the indprod function from the semTools package to create the interaction terms needed for the moderated mediation analyses, as outlined below:

df_moderated <- indProd(ADH_analtbl, var1 =1img1:img3, var2 = provt, match=F, residualC = T)

#final analysis
modmediated_md <- "
  #measurement model
  Ints  =~ img1 + img2 + img3
  #interaction terms created with indProd
  asper =~ img1.provt + img2.provt + img3.provt
  #Structural regression model
   totdp ~ a1*Ints + a2*provcat + a3*asper
 #outcomes
  ART_Adherence ~ c1*Ints + b1*totanx + age  
  a1b1 := a1*b1        #Indirect effect
  Ca1 := c1 + a1b1  #total effect
  ##Index of Moderated Mediation
  IndexOfTRT := a3*b1
"
bootfit_fit <- sem(modermd, data = df_moderated,
                    ordered = "TRT_Ad ",
                    se = "bootstrap", bootstrap = 5000, estimator = "DWLS",
                    verbose = TRUE)
parameterEstimates(bootfit_fit, boot.ci.type = "bca.simple", standardized = TRUE, ci=TRUE)

I would like to confirm whether my approach is correct, particularly regarding the interaction for the analysis, as I’ve come across mixed opinions on this matter and the more I read online about it I get confused. Specifically, I want to know if utilizing the indProd with residual centering is an appropriate method for handling the interaction between the latent variable and observed variable. If it is not, what would be the best way to address this?

I would greatly appreciate any assitance. Thanks!

Hi Sandra,

the first step is to test for invariance (equivalence). If you only want to compare the regression coefficients, you should at least test for configural and metric invariance. If you are also interested in mean differences, it would also make sense to test for scalar invariance. There are various approaches for this. I personally like this one: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29172611/

In this very simple example (which does not exactly correspond to your model), the moderator is tested using a self-defined parameter:

library(lavaan)

# Simulate some data
pop.model.g1 <- "
IV =~ 1 * x1 + 1 * x2 + 1 * x3
DV =~ 1 * y1 + 1 * y2 + 1 * y3
DV ~ 0.2 * IV"

pop.model.g2 <- "
IV =~ 1 * x1 + 1 * x2 + 1 * x3
DV =~ 1 * y1 + 1 * y2 + 1 * y3
DV ~ 0.6 * IV"

n <- c(100, 100)
data <- cbind(
  group = c(rep(1, n[1]), rep(2, n[2])),
  rbind(
    simulateData(pop.model.g1, sample.nobs = n[1], empirical = TRUE),
    simulateData(pop.model.g2, sample.nobs = n[2], empirical = TRUE)
  )
)

# Specify the model
model <- "
IV =~ x1 + x2 + x3
DV =~ y1 + y2 + y3
DV ~ c(b.g1,b.g2) * IV
mod := b.g2 - b.g1
"

fit <- sem(model, data, group = "group", group.equal = "loadings")
parameterEstimates(fit)

Hi Toby,

I'm not entirely sure if I understand your question correctly, so please take my answer with a grain of salt.

For a two group model, the mean difference of the latent variable (Y) is, in principle, identical to the result of a regression where the group variable (X or group, as you label it) serves as the IV and the latent variable (Y) as the DV. Differences may occur under certain circumstances, depending on the level of invariance.

Suppose you have another latent variable (M) that acts as a mediator between the group variable and Y. You can interpret the multi-group model as follows:

(1) The mean difference of M corresponds to the direct effect of X (group) on M.
(2) The direct effect of X (group) on Y is the mean difference of Y.
(3) The direct effect of M on Y is part of the model.

Accordingly, you can determine the indirect and total effect of X on Y as in a typical mediator model (with X as an exogenous variable). Does this roughly answer your question?

Here is a small example (hopefully without typos):

library(lavaan)

# Simulate some data
pop.model.g1 <- "

M =~ 1 * x1 + 1 * x2 + 1 * x3
Y =~ 1 * y1 + 1 * y2 + 1 * y3
Y ~ 0.4 * M"

pop.model.g2 <- "
M =~ 1 * x1 + 1 * x2 + 1 * x3
Y =~ 1 * y1 + 1 * y2 + 1 * y3
Y ~ 0.4 * M
M ~ 0.3 * 1
Y ~ 0.5 * 1"

n <- c(100, 100)
data <- cbind(
  group = c(rep(1, n[1]), rep(2, n[2])),
  rbind(
    simulateData(pop.model.g1, sample.nobs = n[1], empirical = TRUE),
    simulateData(pop.model.g2, sample.nobs = n[2], empirical = TRUE)
  )
)

# Regression
model <- "
Y =~ y1 + y2 + y3
Y ~ group"
fit <- sem(model, data)
pe <- parameterEstimates(fit)
pe[pe$op == "~",]

# Mean difference
model <- "
Y =~ y1 + y2 + y3
Y~ c(0, NA) * 1"
fit <- sem(model, data, group = "group", group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"))
pe <- parameterEstimates(fit)
pe[pe$op == "~1",]


# Same for mediation
model <- "
M =~ x1 + x2 + x3
Y =~ y1 + y2 + y3
M ~ a * group
Y ~ b * M + c * group
ind := a * b
tot := ind + c"

fit <- sem(model, data)
pe <- parameterEstimates(fit)
pe[pe$op %in% c("~", ":="),]

# MG approach
model <- "
M =~ x1 + x2 + x3
Y =~ y1 + y2 + y3
M ~ c(m.0, a) * 1
Y ~ b * M
Y ~ c(m.0, c) * 1
m.0 == 0
ind := a * b
tot := ind + c"

fit <- sem(model, data, group = "group", group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"))
pe <- parameterEstimates(fit)
pe[pe$op %in% c("~", "~1", ":="),]

the first step is to test for invariance (equivalence). If you only want to compare the regression coefficients, you should at least test for configural and metric invariance. If you are also interested in mean differences, it would also make sense to test for scalar invariance. There are various approaches for this. DV =~ 1 * y1 + 1 * y2 + 1 * y3
DV ~ 0.2 * IV"

DV =~ 1 * y1 + 1 * y2 + 1 * y3

  group = c(rep(1, n[1]), rep(2, n[2])),
